topics.name: Integers and exponents
misconceptions: Learners think adding a negative number makes the total bigger
and that -5 squared means (-5) times (-5).

topics.name: Rational and irrational numbers
misconceptions: Learners think every decimal is rational
or that the square root of two can be written as a fraction.

topics.name: Algebraic expressions
misconceptions: Learners think 3x plus 5x equals 8x squared
and that 2 times (x plus 3) equals 2x plus 3.

topics.name: Expanding and factorising
misconceptions: Learners multiply only the first term in each bracket
think (a + b) squared equals a squared plus b squared
or take out only part of the common factor.

topics.name: Linear equations and inequalities
misconceptions: Learners forget to do the same operation to both sides of an equation
and they do not flip the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.

topics.name: Number patterns and sequences
misconceptions: Learners assume every pattern increases by the same amount
or mix up the position number with the term value.

topics.name: Ratio rate and proportion
misconceptions: Learners add the parts of a ratio instead of using them as shares
or think a bigger ratio always means a bigger answer
They confuse direct and inverse proportion.

topics.name: Ratio rate and proportion (continued)
misconceptions: Learners struggle to identify which quantity is being shared or compared in word problems
and mix up direct and inverse proportion.

topics.name: Financial mathematics
misconceptions: Learners work out compound interest on the original amount every year
or forget to change a percentage into a decimal before calculating.

topics.name: Functions and graphs
misconceptions: Learners read the y-intercept as where the graph crosses the x-axis
think gradient is only about steepness and ignore the sign
and mix up input and output values.

topics.name: Lines angles and triangles
misconceptions: Learners think angles on a straight line add to 360 degrees
confuse congruent triangles with similar triangles
and think the exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles on the same side.

topics.name: Theorem of Pythagoras
misconceptions: Learners add the squares of the two shorter sides when they should subtract to find a shorter side
and forget to take the square root at the end.

topics.name: Surface area and volume
misconceptions: Learners confuse surface area with volume
use the wrong formula for a cylinder
and forget that volume units are cubed.

topics.name: Mean median mode
misconceptions: Learners divide by the number of different values instead of the total count
or think the mode must be the middle value.

topics.name: Probability
misconceptions: Learners think probability can be greater than 1
believe a tail is due after many heads
and write probabilities as 1 in 3 instead of a number between 0 and 1.
